news.title: Ubisoft launches Motherbrain, a new subsidiary focused on AI-driven "gameplay innovation"
news.summary_raw: Ubisoft has launched Motherbrain, a dedicated subsidiary focused on developing proprietary generative AI technology for gameplay.

members.title: Ubisoft launches Motherbrain, a new subsidiary focused on AI-driven "gameplay innovation"

news.body:
Ubisoft launches Motherbrain, a new subsidiary focused on AI-driven "gameplay innovation"
Studio is currently developing "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds"
Ubisoft has launched Motherbrain, a dedicated subsidiary focused on developing proprietary generative AI technology for gameplay.
Announced in the firm's H1 financial results published yesterday, Motherbrain consists of the team behind Ubisoft's generative AI project Teammates, which began playtesting last year.
Ubisoft said the subsidiary is currently focused on developing "smart NPCs with memory and AI game masters that manage large-scale systemic worlds."
"[Motherbrain] aims to serve creators globally, both within Ubisoft’s Creative House ecosystem and beyond, and form partnerships with selected technology actors."
Ubisoft CEO Yves Guillemot added that Motherbrain aimed to "empower creators and open up new possibilities for richer, more immersive and engaging player experiences."
The launch of Motherbrain comes as Ubisoft laid off 166 staff at its Montreal and Quebec studios. Production and support roles were eliminated "to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs."
As GamesIndustry.biz understands, the cuts accounted for less than 4% of the studios' total headcount and included members of Vantage Studios.
"As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs," said Ubisoft.

news.body:
一组数据解码KPL十年产业价值。
11月14日，2026年KPL年度总决赛在五粮液文化体育中心综合体育馆收官，北京WB以4:3的比分击败北京JDG夺冠，为KPL创办十周年落下关键赛事注脚，这十年间，KPL已经累计完成3,883场系列赛、线下累计入场192万人次。赛场之外，还有一组数据却直接凸显出KPL这十年商业价值的成长。
第一财经报道，本届总决赛横跨广州、长沙、成都三城，全赛段121263张门票全部售罄；2026年KPL全年平均门票售罄率达92%，决赛阶段达99%。
去年落地北京鸟巢的2025年KPL年度总决赛，就已经以62196名现场观众创下单场电竞赛事现场观众人数吉尼斯世界纪录，该数字甚至能挤进2004年创立的中超联赛单场观众人数纪录的历史前五。达成这一成绩，KPL只用了十年时间。
历经十年发展，不难看出，KPL已从赛事IP延伸出多元商业形态，线下落地“奇妙日”、城市快闪店、影院观赛等场景，线上推出团综、选手IP衍生及游戏内皮肤，构建全场景消费链路。十年间KPL累计携手57个品牌达成商业合作，并且有9家品牌连续三年与KPL稳定合作。还有与包括儒意电影、烤匠等在内的品牌打造定制化联动，其中儒意电影在国庆假期7天内，KPL联名商品销量就超过100万件，KPL也将这强劲的赛事热度转化为充实的落地消费。
不仅如此，赛事还为城市注入文旅客流，近三年来，KPL决赛的外省观众占比高达80%，比例已经超过不少顶级文体活动，正在成为大型赛事最直观的人气指标，2025年在鸟巢举办的年度总决赛，对住宿、餐饮、交通、游览、购物和娱乐等六类消费的拉动效应估值更是高达3.69亿元，对比2026年鸟巢举办的万人以上大型赛演及冰雪活动，单场平均约2.5亿元，3.69亿相当于其1.5倍。
截至2026年，王者电竞顶级赛事决赛已先后落地全国18城，未来有机会进入更多尚未举办过KPL赛事的城市，这也是一场电竞与城市双向赋能格局标杆表现。

news.title: Where 3D meets the real world: highlights from Unity Industry Summit Munich 2026
news.summary_raw: Unity Industry Summit 2026 recap: customer sessions from Mazda to Lufthansa, an F1 simulator, 13 demo stations, and talks on AI agents, robotics, and 3D data.

members.title: Where 3D meets the real world: highlights from Unity Industry Summit Munich 2026

news.body:
Where 3D meets the real world: highlights from Unity Industry Summit Munich 2026
Subarna Ganguly Marshall - Unity
Picture one room and a very unusual guest list. A carmaker shaping its next cockpit. A crane maker moving simulation into the browser. A cargo airline training ground crews in VR. A fusion lab rehearsing reactor operations before building anything. What do they share? All of them build with Unity, and in October 2026, they met in Munich, traded ideas, and left energized about where real-time 3D goes next.
Unity Industry Summit Munich 2026 took place on October 7 at the Munich Marriott City West, bringing nearly 200 customers, partners, and Unity experts together around real-time 3D, and an exclusive Meta VR Glasses feedback lab. Meta was the event’s title sponsor.
Why industrial AI starts with 3D data
Customers have already invested heavily in computer-aided design (CAD) and product lifecycle management (PLM), so the question is no longer whether to invest in 3D, but whether that investment is paying off.
Speakers looked ahead to physical AI, the next frontier. When the work involves people and heavy machinery, “close enough” does not cut it, and answers need to be accurate and deterministic. That means grounding AI in 3D data, which too often sits in silos across PLM systems, factories, and design teams. Unity’s platform turns that fragmented data into secure, structured 3D data at scale.
Unity leaders in their keynote address described three ways to use AI with Unity: curated partner models from the editor, a team’s own approved AI driving Unity with full project context, or trained models running on device. Admins stay in control throughout.
Tools are also already changing daily work. Pipeline Automation pushes a PLM update straight into a live application. 3D data streaming lets heavy models run in real time, even on an aging factory tablet. And Simulation Pro, now in early access, lets robotics teams validate robots thousands of times in a virtual world before a single unit touches the real floor.
Watch the full Unity leadership keynote here.
What AI agents and simulation can do with Unity today
Unity experts Simon Nagel and Jerome Maurey-Delaunay presented their AI agents and workflows flagship demo where they showed how people and AI agents can work side by side on the same project. In the demo, an agent built a 3D configurator from a single prompt, changed an automotive human-machine interface (HMI) on a tablet in plain language, and turned a whiteboard sketch into a repeatable pipeline for CAD data.
Henning Linn, Head of Automotive at Unity, made the case in his automotive introduction and flagship demo that in the car, the screen is the new face of the brand. Brian McGovern, Senior Director, Strategic and Emerging Business, and Daniel Bierwirth, Senior Solutions Consultant at Unity, took robotics from pilot to production with live Simulation Pro demos. Eoghan O’Sullivan, Director, Technical Product Management at Unity, shared a roadmap for Unity Asset Manager, Unity Asset Transformer, and Unity Pipeline Automation.
- Watch the full AI agents and workflows flagship demo here
- Watch the automotive introduction and flagship demo session here
- Watch the robotics: from pilot to production session and Simulation Pro here
- Watch the roadmap session on Unity Asset Manager, Unity Asset Transformer, and Unity Pipeline Automation here
From cockpits to fusion reactors: how eight customers achieved real returns from Unity
Eight Unity customers explained what problem they solved, why they chose Unity, and what changed across two industry-focused tracks.
HMI showcase: From design to drive
The screen is now the face of the product, and Mazda, TomTom, Unicontrol, BMW Group, and Renault are chasing the same prize: the right information at a glance, smooth performance on real hardware, and a clean path from design to production.
- BMW Group discussed how it replaced scattered assets with one shared source of 3D data in Unity Asset Manager, raising the share of requirements met from 59.7% to 85.9% in 21 months.
Watch BMW’s full presentation here.
- Renault traced its path from the Emblème concept car toward series production, with two short optimization sessions cutting frame time by 90%.
Watch Renault’s full presentation here.
- Mazda shared how a human-centric approach and a dedicated in-house Unity team shaped the new CX-5 cockpit, from the 2024 partnership to the 2026 launch.
Watch Mazda’s full presentation here.
- TomTom asked why most drivers still prefer their phones to built-in navigation, then showed how beautiful, relevant, and real maps can win them back.
Watch TomTom’s full presentation here.
- Unicontrol discussed how it built its machine-control app on Unity so excavator operators can read colored bars at a glance instead of numbers, and it feels like a game.
Watch Unicontrol’s full presentation here.
Industry showcase: From design to deploy
PALFINGER, NMY with Lufthansa Cargo, and CEA each took cost, delay, and risk out of the real world. Crane capacity now lives in a browser, loading supervisors can train without waiting for a live flight, and nuclear fusion teams can rehearse reactor operations in simulation.
- PALFINGER outlined how it moved its PALSHOW crane simulation into the browser with Unity WebGL, giving sales teams instant lifting capacity and enabling 12 or more releases a year, up from two or three.
Watch PALFINGER’s full presentation here.
- CEA, France’s Alternative Energies and Atomic Energy Commission, took a deep dive into how it rehearses fusion reactor maintenance in Unity-powered simulation scenarios to cut unnecessary steps and costs, reduce radiation exposure, and build just one full-scale mockup.
Watch CEA’s full presentation here.
From an F1 wheel to the factory floor: 13 demos you could touch
Thirteen demo stations kept the conversation going through lunch, the breaks, and the closing reception, and the F1 simulator was the centerpiece. Attendees queued for a turn at the wheel, an actual steering wheel from a Formula One car. Around it, Unity’s other stations covered a new HMI template, a robot arm running a pick-and-place task powered by an inference model, factory planning with a live lidar sensor, CAD to real time, and a new design-to-Unity workflow with AI agent tooling.
Seven partner stations stretched the range even further. ART S.p.A put visitors in a VR headset to try its V-Cockpit HMI while the crowd watched on a big screen. Paradox Cat showed its HMI and data pipeline work, and Magna rolled in a full VR simulator for user interface and driver-assistance simulation.
Visometry demonstrated AR on a tablet anchored to physical tracking targets, CMC paired a real robot with a simulation and VR station, ROUVY set up two smart bike trainers for indoor cycling, and realvirtual.io ran industrial digital twins inside the Unity Editor. Meta, the event’s title sponsor, offered an on-site feedback lab that let attendees try the new Meta VR Glasses ahead of their early 2027 launch.
Unity Industry Summit’s takeaway: your next breakthrough is closer than you think
One attendee called the day “one of the best events I ever attended, short, concise presentations, diverse demos nicely packed together.” The common thread was clear. When 3D data is no longer stuck, one platform can power almost anything a team can imagine.
Discover more Industry customer success stories on the Unity resources hub to see which one inspires your next project, or visit the Unity Industry page to learn how to get started.
The next breakthrough might already be sitting in your CAD folder.
The question is what you will build with it.

news.title: Phone or computer? How to plan your video game controls
news.summary_raw: Plan video game controls for phone and computer in six steps, from mapping actions to testing on real devices, before your first Unity Spark prompt.

members.title: Phone or computer? How to plan your video game controls

news.body:
Phone or computer? How to plan your video game controls
Unity Team - Unity Technologies
Choose your input devices before you build, and you shape what players can do and how comfortable they feel doing it.
Video game controls are the inputs players use to act in your game, such as taps, key presses, and controller buttons. Picture a small robot hopping across a gap between two floating platforms. On a phone, you tap a button with your thumb. On a laptop, you press the spacebar. If you plug in a controller, you press a face button. The game is the same, but each device changes how it feels, what you can ask players to do, and how long they can play before their hands get tired.
That’s why controls matter. They’re how players talk to your game, and they set the limits of what players can do in it.
When you create a game with a tool like Unity Spark, Unity’s AI-native game creation platform, you describe your game in plain language. You don’t write input code or learn a traditional game engine, but you still make the decisions an engine normally forces on you, and controls are one of them. Your players will open your game on a phone, a desktop, or a laptop, so you’ll plan for two main setups: touch, and keyboard and mouse. A controller is an optional extra.
Work through these six steps before your first prompt, and you’ll write a clearer request and build a game that more people can enjoy.
1. Start with verbs, not buttons
List what your player does in your game: move, jump, aim, pick up, confirm. Keep it to three to five actions for your first game. Then decide which device triggers each one.
Developers who work in the Unity Engine follow the same order. The Input System separates an action, such as “Jump,” from the controls that trigger it, and it groups actions by context, such as one set for walking and another for driving. With Unity Spark, you don’t need to set any of that up yourself, but you can borrow the habit. Write “the player jumps” first, and decide later whether a tap, a spacebar press, or a button does the job.
2. Match each device to your actions
Every device is good at some things and awkward at others. Your players will most likely use one of two setups: a phone, where they touch the screen, or a computer (a desktop or laptop), where they use a keyboard and a mouse or trackpad.
On a phone, players control your game by touching the screen. Touch works best for taps, drags, and short sessions. Thumbs also cover part of the screen, so give them room. The Xbox Accessibility Guidelines suggest making each on-screen button, called a touch target, at least 15 mm square on a phone, and spacing buttons far enough apart that players don’t hit the wrong one. Leave a little empty space around each one so a slip doesn’t trigger its neighbor. Also, consider supporting both portrait (held upright) and landscape (held sideways) play, because some players mount their phones in a fixed position.
On a desktop or laptop, players use a keyboard and a mouse, or a trackpad, the touch-sensitive pad below a laptop keyboard. A keyboard gives you plenty of keys, and a mouse points precisely, which suits games with many actions or fast aiming. Keyboards also ask more of players, who must learn where each key sits, so keep your list of keys short. Some players can’t use a mouse, so offer a keyboard option for anything you ask a mouse to do. Many laptop players use a trackpad instead of a mouse, so avoid actions that demand fast, precise pointer movement.
A controller, also called a gamepad, is optional here. It’s the handheld device with thumbsticks, the two small joysticks, and buttons that console players use, and it can connect to a phone or a computer. Players need to own one and set it up first, so treat controller support as a bonus, not a requirement. If you do support one, avoid designs that need both thumbsticks, the two small joysticks, at once. According to the Xbox guidelines, even shooters can offer a single-stick option.
3. Design for two devices, and say which comes first
Decide which device matters most to your game, and write it at the top of your design brief. Unity Spark is a way to make and share games in a browser, so your players can open your game on either a phone or a computer. Design for your main device first, then check that the game works on the other one. The Game Accessibility Guidelines list support for more than one input device as a recommended feature.
Write each action once, then map it twice: one touch version and one keyboard-and-mouse version. Then look for actions that have no match on the other device. A pinch has no keyboard equivalent, and a mouse hover has no touch equivalent. The Xbox guidelines recommend making sure players can operate content without multi-point gestures, so give every pinch a simple alternative, such as a zoom button.
4. Check speed, complexity, and duration
Letting players remap buttons helps, but it doesn’t remove every barrier. The Xbox guidelines name three more things to check:
- Speed: How fast must players press? A close-range fight that needs rapid presses excludes anyone who can’t tap quickly, no matter where the buttons sit.
- Complexity: How many inputs must players use at once, or remember in order? A combo of several keys in a set order blocks players who can’t memorize it, even after remapping.
- Duration: How long must players hold a control? Holding a key or a finger down to accelerate through a three-minute race tires players out on any device.
For a race, a toggle that keeps the car accelerating solves the problem. You can apply the same idea to sprinting, firing, and repeated jumping.
Unity’s guide to video game accessibility basics offers further insight into hearing, vision, motor, and cognitive needs.
5. Build in forgiveness
Players will miss, slip, and tap the wrong thing. Plan for it:
- Act on release: Activate controls when the player lifts a finger or releases the mouse button, not when they first touch. That lets players slide away to cancel a mistake.
- Skip the gymnastics: Avoid pinch and multi-finger gestures for core actions, or give players a simple alternative, such as a zoom button.
- Offer simpler options: Let players choose how they perform key actions, such as firing automatically, tapping anywhere on the screen, or pressing a dedicated button.
- Teach as you go: Show players their controls during play, and give them a safe place to practice. Both appear on the Game Accessibility Guidelines checklist.
6. Test on real devices and write down what you find
A control that feels fine in your head can feel awkward in your hand. Play your game on a phone and on a computer, and note two kinds of problems separately: accidental inputs, when the game does something you didn’t mean, and missed inputs, when it ignores something you did mean. Then change one control at a time and play again.
Your turn
Open your design brief and finish this sentence:
In my game, players use ___ on a phone and ___ on a computer to ___.
Save it near the top of your brief. That’s a controls plan for both devices, and it gives you a clearer first prompt. When you get access to Unity Spark, include your answer in that prompt, play what you get on a phone and a computer, and note the first control you’d change.
Ready to plan your game’s controls? You don’t need to be a developer. Try Unity Spark, Unity’s browser-based, AI game creation platform that lets you describe your game, refine it in a real web editor, and publish it for others to play.

members.title: 触乐本周行业大事：腾讯网易Q3财报发布，《哈利波特：魔法觉醒》宣布停运，《GTA 6》发售席卷全球市场

news.body:
BLG夺冠影响资本市场，B站就《物华弥新》运营争议提起诉讼，米哈游公布通用游戏AI模型“Gamer”，《明日方舟：终末地》获Google Play年度最佳游戏，TGA 2026提名名单出炉，《影之刃零》获“年度游戏”提名。
腾讯2026年第三季度财报于11月18日公布。网络游戏业务总收入665亿元，同比增长5%。其中，本土市场游戏收入476亿元，同比增长11%；国际市场游戏收入189亿元，同比下降9%。
本土游戏收入增长主要来自《三角洲行动》《无畏契约：源能行动》和《王者荣耀》等产品。《三角洲行动》DAU已突破5800万，上线两年仍在持续扩大用户规模。《无畏契约：源能行动》累计注册用户突破1亿。《王者荣耀》则受益于新玩法和IP联动，DAU及流水均实现同比增长。
海外市场方面，《怪物猎人：旅人》上线后登顶40个国家和地区下载榜。收入同比下滑主要受到去年Supercell旗下游戏热度以及《消逝的光芒：困兽》同期发售带来的高基数影响。
11月19日，网易公布2026年第三季度财报。财报显示，网易第三季度净收入为279亿元，同比下降1.8%；游戏及相关增值服务净收入为229亿元，同比下降1.7%。
从具体产品来看，老产品继续贡献用户活跃度，《率土之滨》日活创下2015年上线以来的新高，《阴阳师》十周年版本登上iOS畅销榜第三，《炉石传说》新资料片上线后升至iOS畅销榜第二。全球化是其中的亮点。《燕云十六声》全球玩家数量已于8月突破1亿，并入围TGA 2026最佳移动游戏提名。《漫威争锋》赛季更新后登顶全球及美国Steam畅销榜。
新游戏方面，网易正在重点推进《无限大》的开发与发行准备，全球上线定档2027年1月15日，当前预约量已突破2700万。生活模拟新作《山海奇旅》，二测定档12月18日，是网易在这一赛道的最新布局。
此外，网易本季度游戏业务毛利率达到74.3%，同比提升约5个百分点，主要受收入分成成本下降等因素影响。整体来看，网易游戏业务收入出现小幅下滑，但盈利能力有所改善。
11月14日，2026年《英雄联盟》全球总决赛（S16）在美国纽约落幕。中国LPL赛区BLG战队在先失一局的情况下连扳三局，以3:1战胜韩国LCK赛区GEN战队，夺得全球总决赛冠军。这是中国战队自2021年EDG夺冠后，时隔五年再次捧起召唤师杯，也是BLG建队以来首次获得S赛冠军。
夺冠消息也迅速传导至资本市场。11月16日，A股游戏板块局部走强，凯撒文化开盘涨停，大晟文化、电魂网络、吉比特等跟涨。
不过，券商分析认为，游戏板块此前已经具备一定的基本面支撑：2026年前三季度，A股游戏板块营收同比增长17.44%，归母净利润同比增长17.67%；第三季度国内游戏市场实际销售收入同比增长5.11%。此外，头部厂商长线运营能力、新品上线周期以及后续递延收入确认，也构成了市场对板块景气度的预期。BLG夺冠带来的情绪催化，与行业基本面预期形成共振。
11月16日，B站游戏发行中心披露，因《物华弥新》开发方龙渊网络单方面终止官方服务器访问并要求玩家迁移至第三方服务器，B站已依法提起诉讼并申请仲裁，同时完成了玩家合法账号、角色数据及游戏资产的备份。B站表示，龙渊网络及其关联公司的相关债务纠纷已经进入司法执行程序，其单方面授权第三方开展游戏运营及收款的行为未经B站认可，并提醒玩家不要轻信非官方渠道的账号绑定、注册和充值引导。
这场纠纷始于10月31日。当天，龙渊网络旗下词牌社工作室宣布接管《物华弥新》的运营工作，理由是研发方与原发行方在游戏运营方向上存在分歧。B站则称，龙渊网络在未提前沟通的情况下单方面终止官方服务器访问，并要求玩家迁移至第三方服务器，涉嫌违反双方合同。双方对运营权变更的说法由此产生分歧，事件进一步升级为法律纠纷。
11月16日，网易《哈利波特：魔法觉醒》工作室发布停运公告，称由于授权协议即将到期，游戏将于2026年12月21日停止充值、停止新用户注册并全平台下架，2027年3月3日正式关闭服务器。官方表示，停运前游戏内常规活动仍将继续开放，相关玩家福利及补偿方案计划于12月21日公布。
《哈利波特：魔法觉醒》于2021年9月9日正式上线，由网易获得《哈利·波特》原著授权后自主研发。游戏上线前预约人数超过1500万，首月流水超过11亿元，是2021年国内首款首月流水突破10亿元的手游新品。上线初期，游戏曾连续多日登顶国内iOS畅销榜和下载榜。运营五年后，这款曾经的现象级产品最终因授权期限问题走向终点。
这也再次引发行业对海外IP授权游戏商业模式的讨论。相比自有IP，授权产品的生命周期不仅取决于游戏本身的运营表现，还受到合同期限、续约条件和版权方决策的影响。即使游戏积累了大量玩家和研发资产，授权到期后，用户、角色及美术资源也很难直接迁移到其他产品。《旅行青蛙：中国之旅》《最终幻想14：水晶世界》等产品今年也相继宣布停运，如何控制授权期限风险、降低对外部IP的依赖，成为游戏厂商需要重新考虑的问题。
11月17日，米哈游旗下《崩坏》系列AI研发团队公布通用视觉语言动作基础模型“Gamer”，能够通过观察游戏画面，自主操作键盘和鼠标，完成2D、3D游戏中的复杂任务。与传统游戏AI不同，Gamer不读取游戏内部数据，也不依赖游戏专用API，而是采集屏幕画面，生成键鼠操作指令，模拟真人游玩过程。在《崩坏：星穹铁道》的实机演示中，Gamer已经能够自主推进主线任务、探索场景和完成解谜。
团队表示，Gamer目前定位为学术研究项目，潜在应用方向包括游戏自动化测试、无障碍辅助和人机交互研究，并明确不支持将其用于游戏作弊或破坏公平性的行为。看来，玩家希望用它来进行“AI代肝”还需要再谨慎考量。
11月17日，Google Play公布2026年度Best of Play获奖名单，鹰角网络旗下《明日方舟：终末地》获得全球「年度最佳游戏」，同时在中国港澳台、东南亚、美洲及欧洲等多个市场获得「年度最佳剧情游戏」奖项。
Google在评语中特别提到了游戏的即时战斗、角色塑造，以及工厂建造与经营机制，认为这些元素共同构成了独特的游戏体验，并将移动游戏的水准推向新的高度。
11月19日，《GTA 6》正式登陆PS5与Xbox Series X|S。20日，R星与Take Two发布最新数据，《GTA 6》的首日全球零售额达到了37.9亿美元，创下了所有媒介娱乐形式中的新纪录。
发售后的关注度同样惊人。数据机构Streams Charts统计，《GTA 6》上线首个24小时，全平台直播累计观看时长达到1.25亿小时，同时在线观众峰值达到791.5万人，远远超过此前《无畏契约》保持的约174万人纪录。游戏媒体评测解禁后，Metacritic评分高达99，发行商Take-Two股价也在发售前上涨超过8%。《GTA 6》的发售已经超出了普通游戏新品的影响范围，成为一次全球性的流行文化事件。
11月17日，2026年The Game Awards（TGA）正式公布年度游戏奖项提名名单。《GTA 6》以8项提名领跑，包括年度游戏、最佳游戏指导、最佳动作冒险游戏、最佳艺术指导等。《控制：共振》和《生化危机：安魂曲》均获得6项提名。
备受关注的《影之刃零》获得5项提名，入围年度游戏、最佳游戏指导、最佳艺术指导、最佳配乐与音乐、最佳动作游戏五个奖项，是本届获得提名最多的国产游戏，也是TGA历史上提名最多的国产单机作品。继《黑神话：悟空》之后，《影之刃零》成为又一款获得TGA年度游戏提名的国产单机作品。
中国厂商继续在移动游戏领域发力。本届最佳移动游戏5个提名中，4个来自中国厂商，分别是：《明日方舟：终末地》《燕云十六声》《异环》以及《怪物猎人：旅人》。此外，沐瞳科技开发的《决胜巅峰》入围最佳电竞游戏。

members.title: 触乐夜话：看AI斗蛐蛐

news.body:
谁更像人类？
这两天游戏圈子里最热门的话题无疑是《GTA6》，我也在玩，但坦白说，进度不快，因为我有个奇怪的习惯：一旦遇到这种开放世界、到处是任务的游戏，古代、奇幻、科幻背景的可能还好点儿，现实背景就特别容易累，一累就想躺着，躺着就没法继续玩游戏——指望《GTA6》移植上Switch恐怕遥遥无期。好在我既不追求速度，又不怕剧透，只要天天玩，总有一天能通关！
而在我躺下休息的时候，一类视频又吸引了我的注意，那就是“AI斗蛐蛐”。顾名思义，是把市面上各个主流或者非主流的AI大模型放在同一个场景里，让它们完成同一个任务，再根据事先设定的规则打分，最后按照分数高低排名。
看过一些之后，我觉得有些UP主的脑洞和设计确实很不错，不仅有节目效果，也有思路分析和成本计算，懂行的观众看门道，不懂的看热闹，当然还有不可不品尝的豆包笑话，可以说是雅俗共赏。无怪乎有人说，这已经不是“AI斗蛐蛐”，完全可以称为“AI综艺”了。
让我比较深刻的有两期：一是让各位AI玩类似“全面战争模拟器”的游戏，几个关卡分别考验了它们攻击、防守、对战、微操等种种能力，相当精彩；二是让AI们两两组队踢足球，相互打比赛，最后按照积分排名，节目效果更是拉满。
在我看来，这些比赛很有趣的一点在于，可以看出AI们“到底有多像人”——虽然目前大多数AI在与人交流时或多或少会展现出一些人性化的态度，用户们还会给它们加上二次元美少女形象，但AI有没有“人类思维”，使用者日常工作中还是有所感受的。
举个具体的例子，“战争模拟器”某一关的要求不仅是全歼敌人，还要保护自己的主帅。主帅血量固定，不会攻击，开局后可以移动。从结果来看，参赛的9个AI在击败敌人的思路上虽有差别，但大致还在“从A到B有3条路，该选哪一条”的范围内。保护主帅则不同，除了失败导致主帅被击杀的情况，成功通关、排名靠前的几位，结束时指挥官都是满血，只有拿了第一名的GPT6.2 Sol，花最少的钱买兵，防守兵死光之后，它让指挥官边挨打边逃跑，同时让高处的弓手持续射击，硬把敌人风筝死，最后主帅只剩26血（满血200）……把主帅血量也当做资源来计算，这就真的有点“像是人在玩游戏”的味道了。
足球也是相似的道理。AI两两组队之后，除了自身实力，与队友如何沟通、配合，最后呈现出的效果是能随机应变，还是简单套路，都是相当有趣的看点。唯一让我觉得有点不合理的是，分组虽然靠的是抽签，原则上是一强带一弱，结果却把GPT6 Astra和GPT6.1 Terra放在了一组，这不相当于让梅西和年轻梅西在一个队里踢球嘛，别的组要怎么玩？
不过，尽管一些AI已经展现出了“像人”的特质，它们玩游戏时的思路和真正的人还有相当明显的差距。拿“造桥省钱”比赛来说，视频发出之后，我经常看的一位《Poly Bridge》“和珅”UP主也去主办方网站上尝试了一下，只是小试牛刀，就轻轻松松破了AI的纪录。最后，他也总结：AI真正的用法，是我们提供经验和脑洞，让它来疯狂试错。只要人给AI一个明确的方向，AI就能去穷举，去微调，直到算出最优解。“AI是个顶级的助手，但还不是脑洞大开的缔造者。”
关于这一点，我也颇有感慨。虽然AI在比赛里各显神通，但从“斗蛐蛐”的效果来看，决定视频好不好看的因素，固然有AI生成的素材，但剪辑、解说、画面、色彩、配乐无疑更重要，而这些全部都是“能工智人”来做的。我不知道未来AI能不能突破这种瓶颈，但至少现在，人的创意显然更重要。
更何况，就比赛题材而言，足够有趣的规则，要么是围棋、五子棋、足球、乒乓球之类传统棋牌和运动，要么是在广大玩家群体里也广受欢迎的游戏，比如炸弹人、坦克大战、贪吃蛇等等，“外交策略”“MC生存”“造桥省钱”更是玩家、主播们流行了很久的热门玩法。只能说，在“能让更多人从中获得乐趣”这个角度，那些已经在多年发展中得到充分验证的玩法还是很有优势的。在这方面，AI似乎还没有拿出更新、更独特、让人眼前一亮的东西。
当然，不论是哪种规则，“AI斗蛐蛐”视频的作者们都会声明，这些AI在节目里的表现只是为了节目效果图一乐，并不代表排名靠前的模型一定更优秀，在实际工作中一定更好用。说实话，这种叠甲反而挺有AI味，尤其是GPT味的。很多人不喜欢GPT这种说话风格，不过我觉得还好，毕竟这种东西之后还能再改嘛。
总之，如果你也正在玩《GTA6》，休息的时候想换换脑子，我很推荐看看“AI斗蛐蛐”，很轻松，没有任何压力，还有豆包笑话，简直不能更合适了！

members.title: 不妙！前暴雪成员团队10年爬塔大作正撞GTA6首发热玩期

news.body:
由Bonfire Studios开发的快节奏团队PvP游戏《Arkheron》即将于11月27日正式发售（以抢先体验形式登陆Steam、PlayStation 5与Xbox Series X|S），这家成立了10年的工作室，终于要交出它的第一款游戏。
Bonfire Studios成立于2016年，联合创始人Rob Pardo是前暴雪首席创意官，担任过《星际争霸：母巢之战》《魔兽争霸 III》《魔兽世界》的首席设计师。2014年离开暴雪后，他和前暴雪成员以及前Nexon北美CEO Min Kim于2016年创立了新团队。
十年只交出第一款作品，在今天的行业节奏里似乎是一种奢侈。且不说《Arkheron》是一款带有MOBA竞技和吃鸡缩圈玩法的爬塔游戏，提供3V3和15支3人团队混战两种玩法模式，也就是说这游戏自带一种用户筛选：喜欢竞技的，喜欢竞技+社交的。当一款游戏把“社交门槛”当成核心设计变量，意味着它不打算讨好所有人，甚至不打算讨好“想一个人玩”的玩家。这在商业上是勇敢的，在增长上是危险的。
但Pardo在今年GDC对外分享中把这段十年历程视为为一场odyssey（奥德赛），并且说了一句很能代表他当下心态的话：“事后诸葛亮总是最容易的，你总会希望自己少走一些死胡同。但因为我在暴雪经历过那么多产品周期，我慢慢觉得，试图在创作上开辟一个新方向，这本身就是代价的一部分。”
一、先有团队，再有游戏
彼此市场对于暴雪前成员出来创业还是有不错的好感，刷脸刷履历就能获取一些资本的关注和青睐。在2016年的初始融资中，Bonfire Studios获得了2500万美元的投资。
Pardo去融资时，甚至没有提交任何具体的游戏提案，只有一些类似《炉石传说》插图的幻灯片。他的意思是应该先成立团队，再根据团队成员的能力/喜好来决定游戏创意方向。他的看法是太多的项目是从一个“大创意”开始再去招人执行，但如果目标是做出真正的东西，顺序应该反过来：因为在团队未形成之前被写下来的那个创意，未必就是最适合这支团队去做的游戏。
通俗一点的讲法是“立项定生死”，Pardo对立项非常谨慎。为此，Bonfire足足用了两年来确立方向。他们的方法是，团队的每个人都能提案，最终他们收到了35个创意种子，方向和元素也五花八门，有吸血鬼like，有受《角斗士》启发的“退伍务农+抵御僵尸”，还要可以买装饰性鞋子的舞蹈游戏……
这35个创意种子又筛选出了7株幼苗，每个都由团队用两三周的时间共同打磨成接近发行级提案的形态，专案回答更深层的游戏循环是什么、哪些内容能让玩家持续投入10、100、1000小时……
Pardo表示这个过程真正的目的不是选出最好的点子，而是让不同岗位的人在同一个问题上对齐：核心概念是什么，参考DNA是什么，游戏基础循环是什么，这个世界提供什么样的幻想。
二、继续探索，找到大奇迹
《Arkheron》改过三次名字：Dungeon Royale、Cult，最后才是Arkheron。
在Dungeon Royale这个种子版本中，故事设定是玩家最终会成为恶魔的囚徒，要为生存而战并逃离地牢，玩家会探索地下城、收集战利品，然后决定是否与其他玩家合作或者是背叛。这也算是个背叛的PvE/PvP游戏。
而当它进入幼苗阶段时，成了Cult，因为团队所有成员都投入了自己的创造力，虽然保持了种子版本中很多相似的元素，但它变成了一个程序生成的地下爬行游戏，核心设定是玩家必须逃离邪教的魔爪，并找到阻止邪教召唤恶魔的方法。在这一过程中，玩家会找到能赋予他们能力的战利品，当玩家们有相同目标时可以选择合作。有时正确的选择是联手击败恶魔，有时是通过夺取同伴的战利品来提高生存几率。最终，只有少数玩家能够幸存、逃脱并获胜。
在这一阶段，Bonfire确定了战斗将是关键，并带有地下城探索元素，但Bonfire同时想要团队PvP，那继续探索。
一开始，项目更偏向于《暗黑破坏神》那种俯视角的点击玩法，但这样无法得到团队想要的快节奏的团队协作，于是《Battlerite》的配方加入进去了，效果更好了，但还是不够美妙，于是他们又在《黑暗之魂》上做了一些实验，但显然团队还是没有找到说服自己往下做的感觉。
后来有一天，团队有人稍微修改了一下摄像机，开始尝试新的摄像机位、操作和响应速度，感觉来了。但工程师的问题也来了，他们一直在为早期的方案构建网络模型，而改摄像机、操作之类的显然需要重写整个网络层，于是服务器框架整个被重写，这个工期需要9个月！并且团队其他成员无法获得技术支持。
Pardo指出，这个阶段他明显犯了一个重大的核心错误：在开始扩充团队之前，没有确保找到一个核心的玩法循环。
当服务器重写，游戏启动开发，每日都有playtest，团队成员给出反馈后作调整和修改。就这样团队经历了疫情，时间来到了2021年。
这个阶段的项目不再是Cult那样的逃离地下城，而是攀爬神秘的高塔。每局游戏开始，15支3人队伍同时进入塔楼，玩家队伍必须通过每层塔楼、夺取道标，这个过程会一直持续到只剩下2支队伍并最终3V3决出胜负。
Pardo表示制作新IP同样是困难的，最初Cult是一个情绪化、充满生机的奇幻世界。真正的转向发生在某次开发会议上，有位美术师问了一句：“如果所有人都已经死了呢？”
这句话把整个项目带去了另一个方向。玩家扮演的将是回响（Echo）——因为未竟之事被困在彼岸的灵魂。玩家将携带一段锚定地的记忆，而这些锚点每个周期都会重新构建高塔，高塔由活人世界的记忆碎片拼成，武器、遗物和神器实际上都与前世中极为重要的选择相连，这些记忆以玩家在塔中的强大能力显现出来。塔的顶端是出路，塔的下方是吞噬一切的深渊。
这个设定最聪明的地方，不在于它有多玄，而在于它替开发团队解决了服务型游戏最棘手的一个叙事难题：为什么同一个关卡要反复打，为什么内容会变。因为记忆本来就不稳定。因为永恒者（Eternals）的历史在被逐渐揭开，而他们的记忆会重塑高塔。于是赛季轮换、地图重组、新套装这些运营动作，在世界观里全部成立，不需要额外解释。
地下城探索的元素保留了下来，但它转向了偏向PvP的元素，玩家在不断探索的过程中，通过打怪、完成任务、打开宝箱、从神庙购买物品、甚至是掠夺其他玩家的物品来塑造角色。
于是，从种子版本到幼苗再到原型，最终留下的那组DNA是《暗黑破坏神》《Battlerite》和《黑暗之魂》：一款面向ARPG游戏和暗黑破坏神玩家的游戏，以PvP为核心，基于吃鸡缩圈的公式打造。
这个组合多少听起来像又一个“缝合怪”的表述，Bonfire花了很多年，才把这这几个标签切实变成游戏机制。
三、物品即英雄，25分钟的“致命抢椅子”
这么说吧，《Arkheron》从《暗黑破坏神》那里拿了俯视角、战利品驱动和套装构筑的骨架；从《Battlerite》那里拿了短TTK、高瞄准要求的竞技场格斗感；从《黑暗之魂3》那里拿了对走位、闪避和“在看见敌人之前先听到危险”的紧张感。而吃鸡缩圈的元素则以一种变形的方式进入：核心玩法模式【登凌】的对局结构是15支三人队（45人）同时进入高塔，逐层淘汰，最后只剩两支队伍在顶层打一场3v3。每层的核心装置叫道标，每一层通往上层的传送点数量，永远少于当前存活的队伍数量。玩家甚至不需要主动找人打架，规则制造冲突——因为慢一步，就没有你的位置了。Bonfire自己给这个25分钟的战局形态起的比喻是“一局致命的抢椅子游戏”。
从试玩反馈来看，这个混合体的高压段确实产生了Bonfire所期望的那种高光密度。信息密度非常大，俯视角自由瞄准意味着玩家需要同时处理自己的瞄准、走位、开宝箱、队友位置、敌方构筑以及环境威胁；而当 15 支队伍在多层空间中同时推进时，战局的噪音会迅速上升。而对于还没有建立起物品认知和地图直觉的新玩家，从“进入高塔”到“真正参与一场有意义的团队战斗”之间的那段路程，可能充满挫败感。
Bonfire对此的解法是【尖塔】模式的引入，这个3v3变体让两支队伍在开局前直接购买装备，跳过搜刮与发育阶段，在几分钟内进入纯粹的战斗循环。从设计意图上看，尖塔模式并不是一个“简化版”，而是一个学习加速器：它把【登凌】中需要经历漫长前戏才能获得的团战经验，压缩成可以高频重复的训练单元。
Pardo透露，【尖塔】模式的诞生来自playtest中观察到的入门摩擦——玩家在【登凌】里花了大量时间搜刮，却在对上第一支敌方队伍时就遭到淘汰，导致本作最精华的团队战斗体验无法被足够多的玩家触及。
玩法模式确认了，那游戏机制呢？
在当下的PVP游戏市场基本上被两套公式统治。一套是英雄射击/MOBA式的“选人—定位—执行”：玩家进入对局前选定一个英雄或职业，然后在整局中围绕这个英雄的技能组去操作。另一套是“落地—搜刮—淘汰”吃鸡玩法：玩家的强度曲线由随机战利品和生存时间共同决定。
《Arkheron》把这两套公式之间的边界给模糊掉了，在Arkheron中，物品即英雄。这里没有职业选择，没有等级继承，没有局外成长。【登凌】模式每局开始都是白板，只有四个待镶嵌的槽位：一顶王冠、一枚护符、两把武器。每一件装备都自带一个主动技能，如护盾/减伤、突进/高速移动、隐身等。捡到什么圣物（通过拾取宝箱或者击败怪物、敌方获取），就临时成为什么。
而这套系统有两层结构。
第一层是成套。同一永恒者的装备，凑两件激活被动加成；凑四件，你会当场变身成那位永恒者，获得第五个技能、更高的伤害与生命值，以及一套改变战斗节奏的大招。代价是：这一局剩下的时间里，打法被锁死在这个角色里。
第二层是混搭。放弃四件套的变身加成，用不同永恒者的散件拼出别人没见过的组合。比如Vaton的鞭子（近战速度、持续伤害）+Penelope的镜子（射速更快、附带减速）。可以说混搭才是游戏常态，这些圣物在不断攀塔中可以随时更换，玩家build是一个持续进行的、由战利品和战局所共同决定的。
也就是说，在《Arkheron》里，玩家需要学习物品之间的搭配效果、套装之间的克制关系，以及在不同战局节点判断该换什么。《Arkheron》把MOBA游戏中传统意义上的角色熟练度和精通感转移到了系统机制的理解和临场决策上。（从这点上看，【登凌】模式的竞技观赏性和团战混乱压力似乎为其接下来能够举办电竞赛事埋下伏笔。）
四、24.99美元，一起玩的朋友才是最贵的
有媒体评价《Arkheron》做好了最难做的东西：手感、音效、打磨以及再来一局的循环，但它的难点它也得解决——有两个愿意一起玩、一起学游戏机制的朋友。
《Arkheron》定价24.99美元，给这个难点再上了一层强度。
Bonfire对游戏定价的解释写得很坦诚，甚至有点挑衅：“我们知道给一款新PvP游戏收费是个很高的要求。当下的每款竞技游戏几乎都是免费的，试一下很容易。但即使是免费游戏，你仍然在投入时间。而学一款新的竞技游戏，要花非常多时间。现在有比以往更精彩的游戏（Arkheron）成为你的心头好，你的时间，比24.99美元贵得多。”
但Bonfire也不是没有做事，还是非常努力地降低了降低了《Arkheron》的经济门槛，为购买的玩家通过免费邀请的形式获得了能和朋友一起玩的更多快乐时光。
其一，好友通行证（Friend Pass）。一个人买，全队能玩。队友下载免费通行证，可以玩教程和训练，也可以加入已购买者的队伍打正式模式，支持跨平台。这直接拆掉了团队竞技游戏最常见的第一道墙——“我朋友不买，我就没法玩”。
其二，首周末全免费（11月27—29日）。没有限制，不需要购买。三天时间，足够一个犹豫的人判断手感。
其三，Xbox Game Pass。从11月27日起，订阅用户在 Xbox Game Preview 的前三个月可以直接玩完整游戏。这是一次用Game Pass换启动量的典型操作。
变现上，他们划了三条线：只卖外观；不做付费变强；不做开箱、不做抽卡。抢先体验期间所有收藏册（战斗通行证）都可以免费肝。49.99美元的Supporter Edition提供游戏本体加两套外观包，后者单买各14.99美元。
这套组合拳的意图非常清楚：用一个不高的买断价，配合“一人购买、全队可玩”的杠杆，去解决新PvP游戏最难的冷启动问题——不是没人知道，而是凑不齐三个人。并且《Arkheron》支持跨平台游玩，玩家邀请Discord社区服务器成员可以免费游玩至12月6日。
但抢先体验也意味着他们自己承认了产品还没至臻至善。官方公告里写得很直接：最优先的是把已有的东西做好——性能、稳定性、战斗手感，以及认真对待bug和外挂；内容方面，他们坦承团队规模不大（去年披露的是70多人），“不要指望成熟长线游戏的更新速度”。
结语
8年的开发之旅，早让Bonfire形成了团队惯例：晨间的游戏测试作为例行公事。而Bonfire的名字也代表着团队的创作隐喻：希望自己创作的游戏成为玩家的社区聚集地。
在2026年推出一款新的PvP服务型游戏，客观环境是这样的：玩家注意力极度碎片化，而新服务型游戏的启动成本（时间、社交、学习）比任何时候都高。以及，《Arkheron》明显是撞上了GTA6首发热玩期。
Bonfire自己对《Arkheron》美术风格的描述是hauntingly beautiful（令人不安的美），既不是暗黑的阴森，也不是奇幻的明媚，而是一种带记忆质感的、被腐蚀过的华丽。它登顶的规则很简单：每一层都要赢，才能去往下一层。
Bonfire Studios 用10年爬到了第一层的门口。11月27日，门开了。接下来要看的，不是他们能不能造出一座塔，而是有没有足够多的玩家，愿意陪他们往上爬。

news.title: Ubisoft misses forecast and bets big on AI development
news.summary_raw: The French publisher plunges on first-half year earnings, though has a few bright spots in its portfolio.

members.title: Ubisoft misses forecast and bets big on AI development

news.body:
In the first half of Ubisoft's fiscal year, ending at the tail end of September, the company fell a precipitous 16.5 percent in net bookings year over year to €644.7 million (~$707.3 million) across the six month period. That fall isn't great news for the developer and publisher, but it's somewhat bailed out by a slight increase in revenue, overall providing a generously mixed financial picture for the fiscal year so far.
Citing an internal reset and restructuring, Ubisoft's earnings report shows that while sales rose in the first half of the fiscal year from €657.8 million to €673.6 million (~$721.6 million to ~$738.9 million), cash generation remains a major concern, with a negative trend in operating cash flow which marked a €323.9 million (~$355.3 million) loss for H1.
For just the Q2 results, Ubisoft reported €389 million (~$426.8 million) in net bookings, beating guidance by €19 million but marking a 16.5 percent decrease year-over-year. For operating income, the company saw a €155.9 million (~$171 million) loss across the quarter, down 24.2 percent from the positive €27.1 million (~$29.7 million) during the same period the previous year.
The Assassin's Creed series proved to be a bright spot for the company's portfolio, with Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced beating expectations thanks to a lot of sales opting for the higher-cost premium editions. Moreover, Assassin's Creed Odyssey saw a slight uptick as Ubisoft credits the release of an unnamed "major summer movie." That movie, though Ubisoft did not outright say it, is likely Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, which was released in July 2026.
The poor financial report is driven at least in part by a weak portfolio of game releases over the last year, a situation unlikely to change with the company's currently announced slate of games that rely heavily on remakes from the Rayman and Heroes of Might & Magic series.
Looking towards the third quarter, Ubisoft is lowering its forecasts, with net bookings now expected to settle in around €250 million (~$274.3 million) in Q3 due to a "particularly crowded holiday season." This revision caused investor confidence to tumble and shares to drop 11 percent on Friday, contributing to an overall 42 percent decline in 2026.
The earnings report also announced a new division within the company called Motherbrain, which spins out of Ubisoft's AI prototype experiences called Teammates from last year. The dedicated subsidiary focuses on middleware AI for the rest of the company, as well as what Ubisoft is terming "smart NPCs" to populate the games. It is unclear why Ubisoft is naming its AI studio after the rogue AI final boss from the Metroid series, but the company looks to be investing into AI game development as a more fundamental pillar in the future.

news.title: Ampere Analysis: Over 2m UK and US Xbox players accessed GTA 6 before official launch by switching location to New Zealand
news.summary_raw: Over two million Xbox players in the UK and US accessed Grand Theft Auto 6 before its official launch by changing their location to New Zealand, according to Ampere Analysis.

members.title: Ampere Analysis: Over 2m UK and US Xbox players accessed GTA 6 before official launch by switching location to New Zealand

news.body:
Ampere Analysis: Over 2m UK and US Xbox players accessed GTA 6 before official launch by switching location to New Zealand
Players on both consoles used this method to experience the title early on November 18, but it was easier to do so on Xbox than PS5
Over two million Xbox players in the UK and US accessed Grand Theft Auto 6 before its official launch by changing their location to New Zealand, according to Ampere Analysis.
Specifically, 1.5 million US players and 600,000 in the UK used this method on Xbox. In comparison, 100,000 US players and 25,000 UK players did so on PlayStation 5.
GTA 6 launched globally at midnight local time on November 19, with New Zealand being the first to access the title.
Xbox players in other regions could switch their console location to New Zealand, restart, and start playing the game hours ahead of others on November 18.
This exploit was more difficult on PS5, as an account's country or region is locked after creation. Players needed to create a New Zealand PlayStation account and purchase GTA 6 through the region's PlayStation Store to access the game early.
GTA 6 has unsurprisingly become 2026's best-selling game since its launch, with projected sales exceeding 24.5 million copies and $2.36 billion in pre-order and launch-day revenue.
According to data from Newzoo shared with GamesIndustry.biz, GTA 6's console-only launch could limit its global reach, as previous data indicated consoles would account for only 22% of global games revenue in 2026.
"While GTA 6 is undoubtedly one of the most important releases of the decade, its initial impact will be concentrated in Western consoles," said Newzoo director of market intelligence Emmanuel Rosier.
"That’s still a big market, which we forecast will be worth $36.3 billion in 2026, but it’s only part of the industry. The longer-term global story will depend on what happens next, particularly on PC and online."

news.body:
This Cozy, Hand-Drawn 2D Milk Delivery Sim from the Minami Lane Developers Is Out
Milki Delivery is an immensely cute, hand-drawn 2D game set in a picturesque countryside. It was co-developed by two independent game creators, Doriane Randria and Dorian Signargout, also known as Blibloop and Doot. Previously, the duo made Minami Lane, a cozy shopping management sim that gained thousands of positive reviews on Steam.
In the game, you play as Neha, a milk delivery worker who rides through the picturesque countryside on her bike. You start a dairy delivery service with your pet cow Milki, and every day, you need to gather food for your companion, deliver milk bottles, and help your neighbors by taking on small quests along the way.
With the money you earn from the sales and the resources you collect as you travel the breathtaking countryside, you can upgrade your bike, your barn, and grow your delivery business. Once your bike is sturdy enough for a longer journey, you can explore more areas where you'll meet new characters and uncover intriguing secrets.
Blibloop and Doot
Blibloop and Doot
Blibloop and Doot
Milki Delivery is a simple, relaxing game that features short dialogues, light resource management, and a fully mouse-driven experience with no hectic tapping all across the keyboard. There is no possibility of failure, so you get to play at your own pace, enjoying the views and the beautiful music written by Antoine Zakrzewski.
"After making Minami Lane together, we wanted to explore something entirely different with a game less centered on management and more on discovery of both a world and its people," developers shared on Steam.

news.title: GTA 6: the first billion-dollar game may also be the last | Opinion
news.summary_raw: What does a billion dollars look like on screen? Or $1.5bn, or perhaps $2bn; estimates swing around a little for just how much money has been spent creating GTA 6. The one thing that’s certain is that it’s the most expensive game ever made – in fact, by far the most expensive piece of media ever made.

members.title: GTA 6: the first billion-dollar game may also be the last | Opinion

news.body:
GTA 6: the first billion-dollar game may also be the last | Opinion
The commercial success of Rockstar’s latest is in no doubt, but it arrives in an industry landscape where risks on this scale are almost impossible to justify for any other company.
What does a billion dollars look like on screen? Or $1.5bn, or perhaps $2bn; estimates swing around a little for just how much money has been spent creating GTA 6. The one thing that’s certain is that it’s the most expensive game ever made – in fact, by far the most expensive piece of media ever made.
The other thing that seems certain is that it was a good investment nonetheless. It had probably grossed billions in preorders alone. News reports are dusting down a nostalgic classic format, “oh wow, videogames are really popular I guess”; this time wide-eyed at the statistic suggesting that GTA 6 alone could outgross every major Hollywood studio combined this year.
Can you see all of that on screen? All those dollars, all those thirteen years of work? Honestly, yes – the sheer scale of GTA 6 is a monumental achievement, a level of richness and detail that players will likely be exploring for months if not years to come before it yields up all its secrets. I’m only a few hours in, but already somewhat in awe of what Rockstar has created.
I also find myself wondering if it’s the last time we’ll ever see anything quite like this.
On one level, GTA 6 was the closest thing to a surefire hit the games industry could ever offer. That’s what justified spending billions in the first place; nobody ever doubted the commercial success of the final game would repay that investment handsomely. Yet in another sense, GTA 6 is an enormous, gigantically risky experiment – one whose results will create ripples across the industry for years if not decades to come.
The climate in which the game is arriving, after all, is a very different one from the world in which it started development. When the ambition of this project was being scaled out, PlayStation 4 was taking the world by storm and nascent live service titles – including GTA Online – offered the promise of a massive new wave of growth for gaming. Budgets were soaring, but budgets had always soared, and besides, money was cheap; low interest rates and strong market fundamentals justified huge investments across the board.
The climate in which the game is arriving is a very different one from the world in which it started development
More than a decade later, the world has shifted underfoot. Interest rates are high enough to make investors wary of risky projects like videogames, and the market fundamentals are frankly rancid. Audience growth has mostly stalled out, and price sensitivity has made it nigh-on impossible for revenues to keep up with inflation. Hardware costs have skyrocketed, making what should have been cheap, accessible console platforms in the sunset days of a generation into expensive systems well beyond the impulse purchase levels of most consumers.
In this climate, it’s no wonder that AAA budgets have come under the microscope more than ever before. Those budgets have climbed to the point where $200 to $300 million dollars is no longer unusual – still vastly lower than GTA 6’s cost, but even at those levels, only the biggest blockbusters can make a profit, and the costs of missing your estimates are eyewatering.
Consequently, where not so long ago the incredible impact of something like GTA 6 would have had other publishers scrambling to follow in its wake with hugely ambitious projects of their own, now I suspect that few if any of them will have the appetite for that kind of risk. The most expensive game in history also seems set to be the most commercially successful entertainment product in history, but the table stakes have almost certainly become too high for even the most ambitious, or arrogant, of Take Two’s peers.
This game doesn’t just need to be a blockbuster; it needs to be the blockbuster
Their instinct to steer clear of this behemoth and not try to follow in its footsteps will only be strengthened if GTA 6 misses any of the gigantic expectations that have attached themselves to it. This game doesn’t just need to be a blockbuster; it needs to be the blockbuster. It has to live up to an incredibly tough comparison with its predecessor, which was one of the best-selling games in the world month after month for many years, and influenced cultural conversations far outside the gaming world for the best part of a decade. GTA 6 will be measured not just on commercial figures, but on the altogether more ephemeral and tricky scale, relevance – and if it fails to live up to expectations on any of those measures, that will change the whole perception of risk around projects of this scale for decades.
Despite the game's incredible launch – both critically and commercially – there are some very apparent headwinds. Console sales figures, dampened by the hardware prices, have not been pulled out of their plunge by the imminent arrival of GTA 6; next year’s launch on PC, likely pulled forward to try to make up for the softness of the console market, will also probably be dampened by the insane prices of PC gaming hardware right now.
The bigger issue, however, is that GTA 6's launch timing was quite obviously designed to take advantage of a cross-generational sales bump, just like GTA 5 did two generations ago – effectively double-dipping across console generations. The timing may have been coincidental, but it looks careful; if the market was working in an ordinary, healthy way, GTA 6 would be arriving just far enough from the launch of PS6 to ensure that most people wouldn’t be willing to wait, but just close enough to ensure that the game was still very relevant and in-demand on the new hardware. That plan has been turned upside down, with the arrival timeline and launch plan for the next-gen hardware itself now looking distinctly iffy; it won’t hurt GTA 6’s sales this year or next, but comparisons with GTA 5’s sales curve may get tougher past that point.
There’s almost no degree of success for GTA 6 that could turn around the structural cracks in the broader industry
This is not remotely to say that GTA 6 is struggling, or will struggle – again, this game is probably going to outgross every Hollywood studio combined – but rather that the weight of expectations resting on its shoulders is immense and may be unrealistic. The nature of those expectations is also important. Ten years ago, executives across the industry might have looked at the performance of a game like this in search of an excuse to greenlight their own monstrously ambitious project. Today, they’re more likely to pick apart its performance looking for any excuse to scale back budgets instead.
That’s because there’s almost no degree of success for GTA 6 that could turn around the structural cracks in the broader industry, or undo the damage done to big-budget development by massively expensive, high-profile failures like Concord, Suicide Squad, or Skull and Bones, to name but three. GTA might be the only brand that could justify a budget in the billion-dollar scale, and no other company seems likely to try to test that theorem; one has to wonder if even Take Two itself would be willing to take a bet-it-all-on-red risk at this scale again with the franchise.
None of this detracts from what the developers have accomplished – but where GTA 5 felt like a taste of the future of gaming when it arrived, it's hard to escape the sense that GTA 6 might instead be a glimpse at a future that will never come to pass. It wouldn’t be entirely surprising if no game budget ever goes past $1bn in 2026 dollars ever again; making this unique and remarkable game into the first and last of its kind, and the swansong for a type of gigantically ambitious and monstrously expensive development project that is only becoming harder to justify over time.

ai.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost

members.title: Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost

ai.body:
Introducing harness adapters: adapt your favorite model to your harness to improve performance and cost
Combining RL on a custom task distribution with your favorite agent harness yields more accurate and efficient models for that target harness and task distribution.
Models are not fully optimized for all harnesses and the tasks you’re doing. Instead, they target general performance. So when you combine a model and harness, you’re leaving performance and efficiency on the table for the stuff you’re actually doing. With RL, you can train a custom harness adapter that squeezes everything out of your model for your harness and task combination.
Take Qwen3.8-27B, its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score with the pi harness is 39% which uses on average 2.9K tokens per task. If we freeze those weights and add a custom RL-trained LoRA adapter we can get 55% pass@1, with average token usage of 1.5K. Most of this is down to the model reasoning less, calling less tools, and performing better first time.
Our earlier work (multi-harness RL, harness adapters) showed that RL on your own task distribution, inside your own harness, gives a more accurate and more efficient model. Those experiments covered data-analysis and code-building tasks. Here we wanted to push this further by exploring whether the result holds at 27B, on harder real-world software engineering tasks, across three harnesses: Pi, OpenCode and Hermes Agent. And most of all, share a fully reusable recipe, so you can reproduce this on your own task, harness, model combinations.
TL;DR
- We trained one LoRA adapter for Qwen3.8-27B per agent harness (pi, Hermes Agent, OpenCode), with RL inside the harness itself.
- Datasets, training and agent rollouts all happen on the Hub in Jobs using TRL's
AsyncGRPOTrainer
, OpenEnv and harbor. - Each harness adapter beats the base model under its own harness on both benchmarks, for both performance and efficiency.
- The three LoRAs are also merged into a single super adapter that runs unchanged under pi, Hermes Agent and OpenCode.
- All artifacts (adapters, GGUFs, RL tasks, safeagents plugin) can be browsed through this Hugging Face collection.

- Testing the filters with short training runs
AsyncGRPOTrainer
for more efficient GRPO training- Training setup
- Super-adapter: merging all adapters into one
- Final results
- Open question: What did the model really learn to do?
- Closing words and future directions
Training inside agent harnesses
We leverage the Harbor integration in OpenEnv and TRL’s OpenEnv guide to train the model inside the harnesses we chose for the final training. We have built ready-to-use docker images for all our RL tasks that come with the target harnesses already pre-installed inside. In our final docker images, we use Pi 1.5.2
, OpenCode 2.2.7
and Hermes Agent v0.22.6
. The diagram below from the aforementioned blogpost explains well the entire protocol:
Most RL frameworks train a re-implementation of the agent loop: the agent is written against the framework's own interface, such as verl's AgentLoop, SkyRL-Gym environments, rLLM's agent and environment classes, slime's custom rollout functions, or ART's client inside your own Python agent. Here the harness runs exactly as it ships, and the trainer learns from the exact tokens it produced, recorded by a proxy between the harness and vLLM. Recent work moves in the same direction: Agent Lightning v1.0 keeps the deploy-time harness in the loop through a proxy ("harnessed agentic RL"), and SkyRL's Harbor integration trains on Harbor trials, converting their chat histories into tokens for the trainer.
Generating custom RL tasks on Hugging Face
For this recipe we created a custom dataset for agentic coding with the Hub, OpenEnv, and Repo2RLEnv. We combined together task retrieval of existing RL envs, task generation with Repo2RLEnv, task validation with OpenEnv, and sampling into a single data pipeline. This gave us the highest quality set of validated and relevant tasks to improve Qwen3.8-27B on agentic coding. In this section, we’ll walk through how we built it, so you can try it out on your own domains.
RL training needs tasks the agent can attempt, a verifier that scores each attempt, and evidence that the verifier is right. A verifier that accepts wrong answers teaches the wrong behavior. A task that is already feasible will not teach the model anything.
This section describes how we built the task set from three sources: two on the Hugging Face Hub and a third generated with Tasksmith, a pipeline in Repo2RLEnv. Every task passes an eligibility screen with openenv validate
, and the same difficulty check against the base model, Qwen3.8-27B.
Three sources
Each task uses the Harbor format, which Terminal-Bench 2.1 also uses. A broad search of the Hub for Harbor environments returned about 59,000 tasks, but they included duplicates, evaluation sets and tasks marked as not for training. We filtered down to just two Hub sources built for training and generated a third set ourselves:
- SWE-smith (Python, Go) injects bugs into real Python and Go repositories, with an LLM rewrite or a mutation such as a flipped operator. The tests that catch each bug become the task's tests. It adds volume.
- SWE-Gym, packaged as Harbor tasks in TaskTrove, turns real GitHub issues and their merged fixes into tasks. It adds real-world bugs.
- Tasksmith generates tasks from merged pull requests. An LLM agent writes the instruction and tests, and Tasksmith checks the result: the reference and a valid alternative must pass, while the unfixed code and a known-wrong solution must fail.
We used Tasksmith to target gaps. We mapped the skills that our target benchmarks test (Terminal-Bench 2.1, the hard subset of SWE-bench Pro, and DeepSWE), then chose pull requests that exercise them, such as HTTP streaming, filesystem operations and serialization. From 30 merged pull requests, Tasksmith produced 24 tasks in 10 Python repositories that passed its checks, 17 of them on a second run. Its checks do not replace ours, so these tasks go through the same pipeline as the rest.
Validation with openenv validate
A metadata screen runs first. It keeps tasks from training splits with permissive licenses. It drops duplicates, tasks marked as not for training, the 253 tasks in our target benchmarks, and any task from a repository those benchmarks use. We then ran the semantic checks from openenv validate
on every task in fresh trials:
- The reference solution earns the maximum reward (
semantic.oracle_max
). - Doing nothing scores clearly lower (
semantic.floor_gap
). - No canary scores more than doing nothing (
semantic.canary_floor
). - A replay of the reference gives the same reward (
runtime.episode_determinism
).
Each trial ran as its own Hugging Face Job, which let us validate dozens of tasks at once. openenv validate
offers the same option for any Harbor task:
openenv validate path/to/task --sandbox hf-sandbox
858 of 1,127 Hub candidates passed. Wrong-answer controls caught defects, including a Tasksmith task that accepted an incomplete implementation and a Terminal-Bench 2.1 verifier (regex-log) that accepted known-wrong answers. Most failures were infrastructure problems, such as images that did not start. Failed tasks stay in a rejected split with the failing check recorded.
Difficulty check with the base model
A valid task can still teach nothing. GRPO (group relative policy optimization) scores each attempt against the other attempts at the same task, so a task where every attempt passes, or every attempt fails, gives no learning signal. Before training, Qwen3.8-27B attempted each task 4 times, or 8 times for a stratified sample of six tasks per repository.
Of 442 scored tasks, Qwen3.8-27B solved 151 every time and 120 never. The 171 tasks it solved only sometimes form the qualified set. The figure below shows how the scores pile up at both ends and how they differ by source. The model solves most Go tasks every time, fails every attempt on more than a third of the SWE-smith Python tasks, and lands in the middle on 73% of the SWE-Gym tasks.
Qwen3.8-27B results on 442 scored tasks. Green marks the qualified tasks, which the model solves on some attempts but not all.
This example shows how we filtered and validated 1,127 tasks to 278 which we included directly in the final dataset. The pipeline then took the remaining 522 rejected tasks, repaired and complexified them with Tasksmith and repeated validation.
Testing the filters with short training runs
The pipeline applies two filters: validation removes broken tasks, and the difficulty check keeps tasks the base model solves only sometimes. This section tests whether those filters change what the model learns. We trained four short runs of up to 50 steps, each on tasks from a different stage of the pipeline, and compared them with the base model on Terminal-Bench 2.1.
Each run trains Qwen3.8-27B with LoRA and GRPO, using TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer
, on 32 tasks. All four use the same agent harness (OpenCode with up to 48 model calls), the same settings and one 8×H200 Hugging Face Job, and the reward is the verifier's pass or fail. The task sets differ in how they were filtered:
- Unvalidated: 24 accepted tasks plus 8 that failed validation.
- Validated: 32 accepted tasks, chosen without regard to difficulty.
- Unqualified: 32 accepted tasks that the base model always or never solves.
- Qualified: 32 accepted tasks that the base model solves on some attempts.

ai.title: Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT-6 Astra
ai.summary_raw: Hebbia tested GPT-6 Astra for financial research. Its prerelease evaluations found gains in source coverage, citation relevance, and presentation quality.

ai.body:
Hebbia sees improvements in financial research with GPT‑6 Astra
Hebbia sees gains in financial research in tests of GPT‑6 Astra.

Before a banker can recommend an acquisition to their client, they need to make sense of financial statements, customer contracts and management presentations. Hebbia’s Matrix helps bring that research together, linking answers to the documents behind them.
Hebbia tested OpenAI’s GPT‑6 Astra to improve two parts of that work: finding the sources a question requires and building a presentation that follows the banker’s brief.
“We’ve been strong partners with OpenAI over the course of Hebbia’s lifetime, and the leaps GPT-6 Astra has made in terms of quality outputs and accuracy have truly been surprising. GPT-6 Astra shines compared to any other model we’ve tested before on these two fronts.”
It could work like this: a banker is helping their client assess a strategic acquisition of an industrial-software company, with roughly 2,000 files to review. What makes its revenue durable? How does it compare with peers? In Hebbia’s hypothetical example, the banker could load the data room into Matrix and examine customer concentration, contract terms and churn in cited cells. Matrix could bring in peer filings and industry news to help develop the deal thesis, then turn that research into a diligence summary and valuation deck in the firm’s template.
In that workflow, GPT‑6 Astra selects documents or Matrix cells to support an answer, then turns the analysis into native PowerPoint slides that follow the user’s structure and guidelines.
“Traceability is really important to our users because they’re basing millions of dollars of decisions on what the AI actually comes back with,” Kavita says. “Citations help with traceability as well as giving users confidence that the AI found the right answer.”
In Hebbia’s tests, GPT‑6 Astra combined broader source coverage with highly relevant citations. It scored 13.6 percentage points above the best alternative tested on citing the required types of sources, while 99.5% of the excerpts it cited were relevant to the question.
Hebbia tested a prerelease build in August-September 2026, using the same financial research cases and grading criteria for each model. Domain experts wrote or audited the criteria against source documents.
“When you’re looking at a data room with thousands of documents, that’s extremely important. Even a single percentage-point gain can yield a lot of marginal benefit,” Kavita says.
A presentation also has to look like work the banker would send to a client.
“I don’t want to create a deck and send that to my partner that looks like AI made it,” Kavita says. “I want it to be made in my firm’s branding, and I want it to look like a human-made slide.”
GPT‑6 Astra led on both following the brief and presentation quality. In Hebbia’s tests, it met 97.9% of the applicable presentation requirements, putting it 14.4 percentage points ahead of the best alternative tested on that measure. Other models traded off polish and adherence to the brief; GPT‑6 Astra ranked first on both.
“In the past, we’ve seen models that really shine on one or the other of these dimensions where they’re really good at craft, but the instruction following and adhering to guidelines is not strong, or vice versa. GPT‑6 Astra is the first model we’ve seen where it’s number one on both of those fronts,” Kavita says.
In Hebbia, users can open a citation to see the underlying document and highlighted passage; slide footnotes lead back to the source material, too. A review could be as specific as checking a customer-concentration figure against the source table and correcting the reporting period before the deck goes to the investment committee.
Hebbia wants bankers to spend less time reformatting decks and checking sources, and more time assessing a deal. Kavita describes what a better first draft could make possible:
“What’s amazing about GPT-6 Astra is its ability to create really precise outputs and artifacts that adhere to user guidelines. You can imagine the hours this will save professionals when you get a deck that is closer to your final output. The overnighters that you have to pull get reduced to a few minutes of reviewing GPT-6 Astra’s output.”
Kavita sees a future role for agents that monitor information in the background and surface signals for finance professionals to assess.
“Imagine getting an important signal a few hours before your competitors,” she says. “You can get started thinking about it and see and process more opportunities that a human is not manually hunting. It can unlock a lot of value for our users.”
Hebbia wants to build on these results to help finance professionals assess deals with research they can trace back to its sources.

members.title: 昇腾算力训出了双榜SOTA的具身世界模型，华为云这次想把整套底座开放出来

ai.body:
昇腾算力训出了双榜SOTA的具身世界模型，华为云这次想把整套底座开放出来
国产算力的成熟，把具身竞争维度从「芯片有多强」，拉入了一个比拼训练效率、数据规模、部署成本和场景落地速度的多维战场。
田晏林 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号 QbitAI
华为云要开源具身世界模型了，一开就是双榜第一！
关键是，这个模型用的还是国产昇腾算力。
11月16日，华为云发布了昇腾原生具身世界模型CloudRobo-WM1.2。
在RoboTwin 2.0和LIBERO-Pro 2.0两项具身智能评测中，它的平均成功率都排第一。
华为云计划在11月30日，开放该模型权重、推理代码和后训练代码。
好么，连后训练代码都直接开源放出，华为这一步确实够猛。
别家机器人团队想教这个模型干个新活儿，不用从零搭训练链路，拿到现成代码，接上自家数据就能直接上手调试验证！
而且这次，华为云没有停留在「把模型迁移到昇腾芯片上跑通」这一步，而是从模型架构、训练框架到核心算子、推理部署，围绕具身模型的特点做软硬件协同优化。
从世界模型预训练、强化学习，到机器人上手干活，华为云把这整条链路接了起来。
这正是「昇腾原生」的核心含义。
国产算力，具身世界模型也能训到双榜第一
首次亮相，华为云具身世界模型CloudRobo-WM1.2就交出了两份亮眼成绩单。
在RoboTwin 2.0和LIBERO-Pro 2.0上，分别跑出88.98%和81.73%，双双拿下第一。
这款模型在昇腾算力上训练，并且其训练框架、关键算子、推理部署，也都围绕昇腾做了优化。
「昇腾原生」，说的就是这套做法。
仿真榜单成绩亮眼，真机场景同样经得起考验。
在第三方独立测试中，5种机器人本体上阵，考了13项操作任务。从转旋钮、双臂连续交接到玩具入篮，模型的平均成功率比第二名高出23个百分点。
有个小细节挺有意思。机器人将插头插入后意外滑脱，CloudRobo-WM1.2可以根据新观测画面动态调整动作，重试插接。
这意味着，它记住的不只是固定动作轨迹，其还具备对物理交互结果的预判能力。
不过，听了华为云在最近举办的具身世界模型CloudRobo发布会上的介绍，我又感觉它能取得SOTA表现，不算意外了。
首先，CloudRobo-WM1.2在「让机器人更懂物理世界」这件事上，下了一些功夫。
常规模型能够识别杯子、定位杯子的空间位置，但学到的大多只是特定视角下的外观特征。
一旦涉及物理交互——比如机器人向前推动杯子，杯子会滑动还是倾倒？这类问题普通模型很难精准预判；在物体遮挡、视角变化、物体动态运动的场景下，误差会更加明显。
华为云采用PPA（Perceive-Predict-Act）多模态世界表征架构，针对的就是这个问题，它把感知、预测和动作放在同一阶段联合训练，同步接入RGB视频、DINO语义特征、深度和三维点云多类信号。
所以，机器人不光会知道杯子是什么、在哪儿，还能理解它的空间结构、运动状态，以及预判动作带来的物理结果。
「杯子被推一下后接下来会怎么动」这种复杂物理问题也能轻松应对。
模型能学的信息多了，具身数据里的动作标注、深度和相机视角却经常凑不齐。少了一项，剩下的还能拿来训吗？
能！
华为云在预训练时用多粒度监督掩码，把缺失或无效的部分从损失计算里划掉。哪部分信息可靠，模型就学哪部分。
这就像做一道综合大题，如果其中某一小问的条件残缺读不通，我们不会直接放弃整道大题，而是先用其他清晰可用的条件继续推导求解。
它的实际意义不在于「容忍脏数据」，而在于让大量不够完美的异构数据进入训练，避免因为局部信息缺失直接丢弃整条样本。
真机采集数据成本高达500元～1000元/时，存量有效数据仅百万小时级别。而头部厂商判断的需求是亿小时级。
在这种供需差下，数据利用效率本身就是工程竞争力。
华为云还在「让机器人有更强的动手能力」这件事上实现了两处突破。
第一，场景理解与动作生成双路径协同，也就是DualAct架构。
一条是action expert动作专家分支，负责直接生成动作，速度更快，适合对响应速度要求更高的任务；
另一条依托世界模型骨干world generator，在理解场景的同时预测未来状态，精度更高，适合精细、复杂、需要考虑物理变化的任务。
而且，两条路用同一套动作目标训练，专家的大小也可以按任务调整，兼顾速度与精度。
第二，本体语义保真跨具身运动建模，解决一套模型适配多形态机器人的难题。
不同机器人本体差异巨大：单臂、双臂、轮式机器人结构各不相同，好比不同车型，操控逻辑各有区别；但同类任务背后，动作意图是共通的。
华为云这套技术，相当于给机器人装个「翻译器」。
模型保留机器人96维、人类运动168维各自的原生状态表征，再用本体标记区分各自的运动接口。
对物体和场景的理解可以一起学；该怎么动，就按机器人各自的结构特征来自主适配。
据华为云披露，现在训练数据已经扩到2.75万小时，接入20个数据源、33种本体。
另外，做具身模型还有一个共识，「想得准」和「动作出得快」挺难兼顾的。
华为云咋处理呢？
给推理方案设置了四个「套餐」——World/Expert Action，Joint/Action-only，四种弹性推理模式可按需组合。
换句话说，可以只输出动作，也可以兼顾输出动作+做出预测；你还可以指定让动作专家来搞定，或是让世界骨干来完成。
研发调试要精度，实际部署要速度，都能照顾到，研发团队可以根据算力、时延的要求灵活组合，就像点菜一样，丰俭由人。
最重的一档，计算量约是最轻一档的11倍。
按任务挑着算，是CloudRobo-WM1.2在模型设计上省算力的办法。
可要把长视频、深度和动作一起训进去，还要让模型到了真机能及时出动作，昇腾是怎么接住这些活儿的？
「昇腾原生」，到底原生在哪里？
华为云先从显存下手。
拿7B参数的世界动作模型算笔账。
光是模型参数、梯度和优化器状态，就要吃掉约112GB显存！
注意，长视频带来的额外开销，还没算进去呢。
具身世界模型对算力的胃口，不是一般的大。视频、深度、三维点云、动作序列，模型都得处理。算力与显存需求远超普通大模型。
到了真机上，又要算另一笔账。机器人等着下一步指令，模型得及时给出动作，推理开销也得控住。
这笔开销牵动的是整套训练系统。
几张卡怎么分活儿，大数据怎么送过去，训练框架和算子怎么在卡上跑，多分支梯度如何归约，attention选择性重算等，都要围绕昇腾这套硬件一起调。
这就是「昇腾原生」。
一张工作台摊不开，就让几张台子一起干。
华为云把数据处理和模型计算分开，前者可以交给鲲鹏，后者由昇腾NPU来做。
多张昇腾卡通过超节点高速互联，长视频序列可以拆开算，模型参数也能分着存。
有些中间结果可以等用到时再算一遍，多花几步计算，给显存腾出地方。
桌子摆开了，下一批数据还得及时送过去。
两路各4Mbps的视频，录8000小时，光压缩视频就有约28.8TB。
训练时还要反复读、解码、抽帧，再把画面对上同一时刻的机器人轨迹。
华为云把视频、关节状态、末端轨迹、底盘和任务标签统一存起来，按一次完整的操作建索引。
搜到一段动作，相关数据就能一块儿取出来。常用的提前缓存，下一批要用的提前读。卡还在算手上这批，后一批已经在路上了，避免算力空等。
这有点像餐馆后厨：热门菜提前备料，下一单还没来，食材已经先解冻了。
数据到了，训练框架还得把活儿派匀。视频、点云和动作占的显存不一样，一批样本分得不好，这张卡已经挤满了，那张卡还空着。
华为云在框架里单独安排重计算，配合长序列和模型并行，把各张卡的负担分匀一点。几张卡要交换结果，也可以趁数据还在路上，先算手头能做的部分。
到了强化学习环节，同样存在算力等待瓶颈。
模型把动作算出来了，仿真里的机器人得照着做，再把新画面和结果送回来，训练才能接着跑。
华为云和清华大学于超团队把开源具身强化学习框架RLinf接到昇腾上，有个改动挺有意思。
在一组LIBERO测试里，模型一次给出10步动作，第10步才需要看新画面。那前9步的画面就无需逐帧渲染。物理仿真一步步走，奖励也照常算，在动作规划周期内减少渲染开销。
昇腾卡上也有活儿能省。
华为云团队把归一化、旋转位置编码等反复要做的运算，接到昇腾NPU的融合算子上。
原来要分几次做的计算，有些可以在卡上合着算。少下几次指令，中间数据也少搬几趟。
华为云透露，适配后，相关推理效率和训练吞吐有约2至3倍的提升。
拆开看RLinf公布的测试，GR00T N1.5和N1.6单位时间内能算出的动作增加了195%至278%，StarVLA的训练调用吞吐提升186%至240%。
一整轮强化学习能快多少，还得把仿真、通信和参数更新都算进去。
这些活儿接到了CloudRobo，也就是华为云的具身智能开发和运行平台。
数据难采，可以先在仿真里合成一批，再在昇腾上做预训练、强化学习和评测。
上真机时，就能用上前面说的四种推理模式。调试时把未来画面和动作一起算出来，现场干活时可以只算下一段动作。
动作算完了，还得及时送到机器人手上。
华为云用R2C（Robot to Cloud）接入不同机器人。现场的画面和状态能传上去，模型算出的动作也能发回来。
需要近距离无线通信时，还可以结合星闪，减少传输延迟。
碰上新的工况，团队会把采到的作业数据带回CloudRobo，看看模型在哪一步出了问题，再补训、评测，把更新后的模型部署回去。
好，模型能训出来，也能上真机了。到了工厂，先让机器人接哪道工序？到了仓库，哪种工况最该补数据？
这些事，天天跟设备打交道的人最清楚。
要把伙伴拉进来
可真要把一道工序教给机器人，谁也没法一手包办。
做模型的进厂，得补现场数据、学工艺。制造企业懂生产，但也得有人帮着采数据、训模型。
本体厂商则要把模型接到自家机器人上，边跑边调。
华为云呢，想把这几拨人拉到CloudRobo上一起做项目。
数据怎么进、模型怎么训、仿真怎么测、真机怎么跑，平台留了API、SDK、CLI和插件接口。
各家的模型、数采工具和训练框架，都能接进来用。
CloudRobo-WM1.2也会进平台，权重、推理代码和后训练代码计划于11月30日开放。
东西做好了，怎么卖出去？
华为云「行业AI梦工厂」具身智能专区依托昇腾云和CloudRobo，伙伴能在这儿发布数据集、模型、工具链和方案。
比如，做仿真引擎，华为云和伙伴一起打磨，做好的能力可以集成进CloudRobo，也能上云商店卖。
华为云具身智能产品线总裁、具身智能Lab主任吴小东还给了句准话：同等条件下，华为云优先推荐伙伴的模型和方案。
具身智能正在走向产业化的关键窗口期，昇腾云已成为国产云阵营中事实上的算力底座与生态入口。
从6月上线到现在，具身智能专区已经和230多家企业及高校开展合作，吸引了超1.65万名开发者，攒下1500多项行业资产。
当前，国内每10家具身智能企业，可能就有8家选了华为昇腾云。
身处国内具身智能市场处于第一梯队，华为昇腾云也完成国内重点高校的大范围覆盖。
浙大、上海交大等都已经和华为云深度合作。他们用昇腾算力、仿真平台和开源代码一起训模型、搭数据集、做评测，也共建课程和实训基地。
产业侧的落地也在持续提速：与福龙马围绕无人环卫展开合作，联合定义产品，也一起搞营销、推上市；与亿嘉和联合发布配网带电作业机器人，在配网高危作业中规模化商用；与山河智能联合推进矿山场景落地……
从工业制造、城市服务、应急救援，到生活服务、医疗康养、教育实训，CloudRobo的触角已经延伸至20多个行业。
One more thing
全球AI的比拼，正从一块芯片的性能，转向一整套系统的能力。
落到具身智能上，电力得供得上，机器人干活的数据得收得回来、用得起来，还得把机器交到客户手里，进了新场景能接着改。
国内有电力基建和「东数西算」打底。国产算力训练具身模型逐渐成熟，接下来比的就是谁训得更快、能用上更多数据、部署成本更低、落地更快。
单项技术能跑到前面，把各个环节接起来的工程能力和产业配套，也一样重要。
用昇腾原生训练的CloudRobo-WM1.2，在两项国际基准上都拿了第一，挺提气的。
至少对具身智能厂商而言，训练侧终于不只有英伟达一条路可走了。

members.title: 双系统决策+双层自进化，Agnes让Agent效率最高提速14倍，成本骤降至1/27！

ai.body:
双系统决策+双层自进化，Agnes让Agent效率最高提速14倍，成本骤降至1/27！
已开源Agnes Harness
一水 发自 凹非寺
量子位 | 公众号QbitAI
过去做一套企业软件，开发可能要花90块，给每家客户适配只要10块。软件做一次、卖给很多家，前面那90块就能被一点点摊薄。这是传统软件公司的生意逻辑。AI把这个公式改了。现在开发只要1块，适配还是10块。
谁懂，独立FDE（前沿部署工程师）、斯坦福在读博士Zaniel此前跟量子位交流时算的这笔账，几乎把今天Agent落地最扎心的现实说透了。
开发成本从90块跳水到1块，最难啃的那10块，却还杵在原地纹丝不动。
为啥？
因为企业适配这事儿，归根结底就是让AI把每个客户的业务流程、工具系统和现场设备重新认一遍。
偏偏现在不少Agent，本质上还是被关在浏览器和终端里的「赛博临时工」。
写代码时天花乱坠，Benchmark分数一个赛一个漂亮。
可真让它走出屏幕，去指挥车间里的传送带、读取工业称重台的读数，或者操作机械臂完成一次精密装配，画风立马就变了。
抱意思，这个我之前没见过，你得重新教我。
经典老番之「上岗了才有工作经验」，我懂，那就仔细教呗。
结果好不容易教会了，转头它又给你来一出「鱼的记忆」——
在同一个客户场景里，第100次执行任务犯的蠢，跟第1次几乎一模一样。
Token一轮没少烧，经验是一点没记住。
气笑了。。。
所以，怎么让Agent快速适应新任务，同时把执行经验沉淀下来？
Agnes Harness。
一个采用Apache 2.0许可证、允许商用，并已在GitHub收获2.1k Star的开源系统，就这样进入了我的视线。
给Agent配上快慢双脑，先把干活成本打下来
先给大家划个重点，Agnes Harness身上最值得看的有两点：
一个是Sys1双系统决策，另一个是TTT×RSI双层自进化。
顺着了解这两个创新设计，你就会明白如今Agent落地的卡点究竟在哪了。
为了让整个过程更好理解，咱们直接原地来一局「重生」（doge）。
△图片由AI生成
一觉醒来，假设你现在成了一家工厂的老板，为了降本增效，你就想着一件事——
我要把AI引进自家工厂。
往市面上一看，模型倒是一个比一个强，但真准备掏钱部署时，第一关就来了：
到底怎么才能把每次任务的执行成本降下来？
AI这个概念再性感，不能最后让我倒贴钱吧，ROI不得先仔细算算。
聪明的你决定先查查账，以前大家都把钱花哪儿了？
一番盘下来，好家伙，最大的开销居然是大模型调用。
现在不少Agent之所以又慢又贵，倒不是大模型不够强，恰恰相反，是因为它太能干了，结果什么活都往它身上塞。
很多根本不需要复杂推理的操作，也要完整调用一次大模型，这不纯纯大材小用浪费吗？？
Agnes Harness就想了，不行，咱得分工，于是干脆搞出了一套「Sys1双系统决策」机制。
需要复杂推理的部分，那就还是交给大语言模型System 2。
而那些高频且明确的操作，则交给专门训练的9B决策模型System 1，也就是Agnes Sys1.0。
它可以通过插件接入Agnes Harness，专门判断下一步该怎么走：
调用哪个工具？继续等待还是立即执行？拿不准时，要不要请大模型出场？
可别小看了这个9B模型，它的「单兵作战能力」相当能打。
Agnes Harness报告显示，在一项模拟家庭漏水的任务中，同样是判断下一步该干啥，大模型平均要想7.6秒，Agnes Sys1.0只需要0.53秒。
速度直接是原来的14.3倍。
至于成本，在另一组行李房（完成物品称重、竖直摆放和暂存）测试中，双方分别完成100次判断，在线大语言模型的单次调用成本约为0.00247美元，Agnes Sys1.0则约为0.000091美元。
算下来，单次决策成本只有前者的约1/27。
有了这一「最强辅助」，两个系统一配合，那不得起飞？？
Agnes Harness还真拉来一只机器狗，在仿真环境中测试了一把。
机器狗的任务是，在室内找到门，然后穿过去。
比起每一步都调用大模型的方式，「大模型+Agnes Sys1.0」这对搭档直接将整体任务耗时缩短了32.9%。
光看数字可能还没啥感觉，但点开视频一对比，好家伙，这速度差距还真是肉眼可见呐。
速度上来了，成本也降下去了。
但新问题很快又来了：
今天换台设备，明天接个新任务，Agnes Sys1.0没见过怎么办？
总不能每来一个新活，就把模型拖回去重新训练一次吧。
好在Agnes Sys1.0还留了一手——TTT，也就是测试时训练。
别再每天失忆，让任务经验真正留下来
怎么让Agent快速适应新任务，一个很自然的想法是：
培训呗。
可问题来了，传统模型微调，得先收集新任务的数据，再训练、部署。
一套流程下来，时间和成本可都不低。
TTT就有意思了，直接让Agent在上岗前突击补课。
Agnes Sys1.0先看看新任务要干啥，再自己出几道有标准答案的练习题，做完后根据结果调整一下自己的判断方式。
整个过程不动9B模型的主体参数，只微调最末端一小组负责校准判断的参数即可。
不过，这场「突击培训」还有个挺有意思的设定：
学完就清空。
啊？好不容易学会了，怎么还给忘了？？
其实是怕它学串了。
毕竟今天操作的是A设备，明天可能就换成B设备，要是每次学到的东西都往模型里塞，时间一长，谁知道会不会互相打架。
所以Agnes Sys1.0干脆每次只针对眼前的任务临时调整一小部分参数，干完就恢复原样。
听着挺有道理，但身为老板，我还是忍不住担心：
模型参数可以恢复，辛辛苦苦摸索出来的经验，总不能也跟着打水漂吧？
这就轮到「双层自进化」的另一半——RSI出场了。
RSI，递归自我改进，这大家都不陌生了。
每次干完活，先给Agent开一场复盘会。
Agnes Harness会把整个执行过程重新过一遍，看看哪里反复报错、哪一步最耽误时间，再调整Prompt、Memory、Skills和Subagent的配合方式。
如果发现了更好的方法，就先在当前任务中验证效果。
确认确实有效后，再整理成版本化Playbook（操作手册），留给后续任务直接复用。
Agnes Harness还真拿一个复杂设备入库验收任务试了一把。
简单来说，设备进了仓库，Agent得按流程操作称重台、读取重量，再完成验收。
第一次，Agent不出意外地翻车了。。。
称重台还没稳定就急着读数，操作顺序也没安排明白，折腾了整整30分钟，最后还是超时了。
但这次的坑，RSI给记下来了。
结果第二次再来，直接按照验证过的流程走。
不到8分钟，搞定。
注意，AI总结出来的新方法，得先经过仿真测试，确认靠谱了，才能写进Playbook。
就，允许你自己进步，但别拿我的设备试错啊。（doge）
到这儿，Agent总算不再是个每天从零开始的「赛博临时工」了。
但等等……
在屏幕里练得再熟，到了工厂现场，总不能靠鼠标去拧螺丝吧？
让Agent走出屏幕，就是现在。
走出屏幕，给Agent补上连接现实世界的身体
不过，给Agent补身体，可不是上来就装机械臂。
真要进厂干活，得先跟现有的业务系统打好交道。
订单、仓储、审批……每家工厂都有自己的一套流程和工具。
总不能接一个客户，就重新魔改一套Agent吧？？
Agnes Harness的办法倒也实在：
做成插件，按需装配。
业务工具、模型适配器、Agent工作流、Skills，甚至操作界面，都能封装成插件。
已有的业务系统，也可以通过MCP直接接进来。
说起来有点抽象，我干脆自己上手试了一把。
Agnes Harness目前还没有现成的在线网页版，想体验得先在本地部署。
门槛倒不算高，准备好Node.js 24.10及以上版本和pnpm 10.34.5即可，使用云端模型API的话不用额外配GPU。
那就简单了。
直接把GitHub地址扔给DeepSeek Harness，让AI帮我装AI不就得了。（doge）
我继续在旁边码字，大约50分钟后，Agnes Harness就在我的MacBook Air上跑起来了。
进入工作台，先选模型。
可以用项目提供的Demo模型，也能配置自己的模型API。
我直接接上了平时常用的模型。
接下来，该整点实际的了。
我顺手攒了一个审稿插件，用来检查错别字、语病、前后矛盾和数字单位问题。
需求说完没多久，插件就出现在待审列表里。
人工确认代码和权限没有问题后，点击启用，状态随即变成了「本地」「就绪」。
那就试试呗。
我随手扔进去一段故意埋了坑的稿子。
好家伙，还真揪出了6处问题，连位置、问题类型和修改建议都给标出来了。
更有意思的是，新开一个对话窗口，只要说一句「帮我审稿」，Agent就能自动调用这个插件。
不用每次重新交代检查规则。
而且插件还有版本管理机制，新会话可以使用新版本，正在执行的任务则继续沿用原来的版本。
这下，插件化的好处就很直观了。
今天装进去的是审稿工具，换到工厂里，也可以是订单查询、仓储审批。
一次做好，以后接着用。
你以为到这儿就完了，大No特No，真正的硬骨头还是硬件。
机械臂、机器人、传感器，又该怎么听懂Agent的安排？
Agnes Harness的办法，是给这些设备定一套统一的「沟通规则」，它叫MHS（Model Hardware Standard，模型硬件标准）。
设备接入后，先按照统一格式「报家门」：
我现在是什么状态，能执行哪些动作，又能返回什么数据。
至于先调用谁、后调用谁，任务又该怎么拆，则交给Agnes Harness统一安排。
官方还做了一个火星救援Demo。
Agent接到救援任务后，先派出搜索设备寻找宇航员，再协调机器人和气闸，把人安全带回基地。
找人、开门、移动、返回。
多个设备围着同一个目标接力干活，Agent这回终于不只是在屏幕里点鼠标了。
不过，真涉及物理设备，安全可不能开玩笑。
Agnes Harness负责安排任务，实时控制和物理安全仍由设备控制器负责。
目前，MHS正在以官方插件形式接入Agnes Harness的新版本。
到这儿，Agnes Harness这套系统，算是从头到脚捋了一遍。
大语言模型负责思考，Agnes Sys1.0负责快速判断，TTT适应眼前的新任务，RSI留下长期经验，插件和MHS则负责连接软件系统与真实设备。
好家伙，这一套组合拳打下来，成绩到底怎么样？
官方晒出了一份覆盖9项基准的阶段性自评成绩单。
9项评测，6项拿下对照组第一，另有1项与Codex并列第一。
具体来看，考验复杂任务规划的DeepPlanning，Agnes Harness拿下87.07分；拼复杂代码能力的BigCodeBench-Hard V1，通过率达到40.69%。
这成绩一摆出来，咱这个工厂老板终于有点盼头了。
以后花钱请AI来干活，总算不用天天跟在屁股后面收拾烂摊子了。（doge）
让每一次交付，成为下一次交付的起点
就挺感慨。
年初，老板们还在FOMO，生怕自家公司接入AI慢了一步。
现在再翻翻网上的讨论，画风已经有点不一样了。
有人开始吐槽，AI Agent完成前80%的任务时宛如魔法，最后20%却能让自己调试整整4个小时。
还有人更惨，一位SaaS从业者称自己每月收客户400美元，却被报错的Agent在不到6小时内疯狂重试3.1万次，一夜烧掉4700美元Token，直接倒贴十几倍。
甚至连AI行业的高管也顶不住了。
Cyera首席战略官Sol Rashidi此前透露，自己已经裁掉了一半Agent。
原因很简单：
花在盯着AI干活上的时间，比AI替自己省下的时间还多。
这就多少有点尴尬了。。。
只能说，潮水退去之后，大家最后看的还是经济账。
一个Agent从进场，到运行、维护，再到复制，每一步都可能产生新的账单。
而Agnes Harness正在尝试的，正是把这四本账一笔笔往下压。

尤其是最后一笔：
复制。
单个项目省钱是一回事，前一个项目的投入，能不能变成下一个项目的起点，又是另一回事。
就像开头Zaniel算的那样，AI已经把开发成本从90块打到了1块，剩下那10块，才是真正难啃的骨头。
如果今天跑通的流程、踩过的坑和积累的经验，都能留下来，变成下一次交付可以直接复用的能力，这10块就有机会被一点点摊薄。
而Agnes Harness走的，正是这条从10到0的路。
